root_cause.text: In XFS quota scrub, xchk_quota_item had an error-handling early-return path after xchk_fblock_process_error that exited while still holding the dquot mutex dq->q_qlock, causing a lock leak and potential deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `mutex_unlock(&dq->q_qlock);` immediately before `return error;` in `fs/xfs/scrub/quota.c`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that when `xchk_fblock_process_error` returned false, `xchk_quota_item` returned without dropping `dq->q_qlock`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release dq->q_qlock before the error-path return to fix a missing unlock that could leave the quota mutex held.
intent_record.what: A block was added around the early-return path after xchk_fblock_process_error(sc, XFS_DATA_FORK, offset, &error), inserting a mutex_unlock(&dq->q_qlock) call before returning error.
intent_record.how: When xchk_fblock_process_error indicates the function should return early, the quota lock q_qlock is now released first, preventing the function from exiting while still holding the mutex and avoiding lock leaks or subsequent deadlock/hang behavior.

candidates.rationale: This early return is the direct lock-leak site: on the error path after xchk_fblock_process_error, it exits xchk_quota_item while dq->q_qlock is still held, causing the missing unlock and potential deadlock.
This condition gates the buggy early-return path. When true, control flows to the immediate return without releasing dq->q_qlock, enabling the lock leak.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
xfs: check the ondisk space mapping behind a dquot

Each xfs_dquot object caches the file offset and daddr of the ondisk
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 7d1f0e167a067ed741dec08b7614d76893422b04
Author: Darrick J. Wong <djwong@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Dec 15 10:03:44 2023 -0800

    xfs: check the ondisk space mapping behind a dquot
    
    Each xfs_dquot object caches the file offset and daddr of the ondisk
    block that backs the dquot.  Make sure these cached values are the same
    as the bmapi data, and that the block state is written.
    
    Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <djwong@kernel.org>
    Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact error-handling path in `xchk_quota_item` around the newly added bmap check and lock transitions. The vulnerable construct is present: after reacquiring the dquot lock with `xfs_dqlock(dq);`, the function calls `error = xchk_quota_item_bmap(sc, dq, offset);`, then only unlocks the inode with `xchk_iunlock(sc, XFS_ILOCK_SHARED);`, and immediately checks `if (!xchk_fblock_process_error(sc, XFS_DATA_FORK, offset, &error)) return error;`. On this early return path, there is no `xfs_dqunlock(dq)` before returning, so the function can exit while still holding `dq->q_qlock`, matching the root cause. There is no visible fix here such as unlocking the dquot before the early return or restructuring control flow to ensure the dquot lock is released on all exits. Therefore the function contains the bug and is not yet fixed.

The root cause is an early return after xchk_fblock_process_error while still holding dq->q_qlock. That vulnerable construct is present here. The function explicitly drops and reacquires the dquot lock: "xfs_dqunlock(dq); xchk_ilock(sc, XFS_ILOCK_SHARED); xfs_dqlock(dq);".
